summary: Feed s160_double to IDS is degraded: 12.6% duplicate packets and 19.4% one-way TCP sessions (26/134). IDS requires both directions and full payload for stateful detection - both faults reduce detection coverage and waste tool capacity.

findings.root_cause: 19.4% of TCP sessions are one-way (26 of 134), exceeding 10% threshold. Most likely asymmetric routing combined with packet broker load-balancing without flow affinity, or SPAN/TAP covering only one direction, so client->server and server->client are sent to different tool ports or one direction is missing entirely.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and stateful signature matching. One-way flows prevent stream reassembly, break detection of exploits that span request/response, and cause high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker aggregation / flow-aware hashing to deliver both directions of each session to this same 1G IDS port, ensuring complete bidirectional flows for detection.

findings.root_cause: 12.6% of packets are duplicates (283 of 2243, threshold 5%). Typical cause is overlapping SPAN sessions, tapping both sides of a link, or aggregating multiple TAP feeds without broker deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates waste IDS 1G capacity and processing, inflate flow counts, distort analytics, and can trigger false positives or cause resource exhaustion that masks real attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication (packet hash window) before delivery to IDS to drop identical copies while preserving one complete copy of each packet.
